Attempt 1 PASSED the full rubric and was approved. The orchestrator then reverted it to DRAFT deliberately -- not a defect report -- to bring RFC 5545 3.1 line folding into scope. The plan had deferred folding as a residual risk on the correct observation that neither AC-7 nor AC-8 names it; the plan-reviewer confirmed that is no rubric failure and recorded the deferral in the honest shape the process asks for. Two arguments carried the reversal: the 75-octet threshold is the MEDIAN case for accented pt-BR titles rather than an edge case, and the deferral's load-bearing premise (that Google's importer tolerates unfolded lines) was asserted without a citation in a plan otherwise disciplined about sourcing. The scope reading is that AC-7 already requires 'CRLF line endings per RFC 5545', and CRLF and folding are the same section of that RFC, so folding was inside AC-7 rather than an expansion of it.

Approved once, then re-reviewed after a late addition, because the first verdict no longer described the file on disk. The addition closed a gap the test-reviewer had flagged as real while correctly noting it mapped to no rubric id: escapeIcsText was going untested, though the plan's own risk table had expected a title carrying RFC 5545 TEXT-reserved characters. An unescaped comma in SUMMARY can be read as a value separator, and 'Comprar pao, leite e cafe' is ordinary owner data. Neither the folding test nor the escape test covers their interaction, which is why the code review was asked to read the call order directly.

Level 1 failed on a noUncheckedIndexedAccess type error inside test/export-ics.test.ts, which R-X forbade the Implementer from fixing. It stopped and reported with correct attribution, exactly as in phase 1. SECOND occurrence of the same class: a test file authored test-first that runs green under vitest (transpile-only) but fails tsc -b, discoverable only after the seam exists because tsc fails earlier on unresolved imports. Phase 1 was exactOptionalPropertyTypes; phase 2 was noUncheckedIndexedAccess. Root cause is that the test pair is never told this project's strict tsconfig flags. Mitigated by instruction both times; the systemic fix -- recording the flags where the test pair reads them, e.g. docs/context/testing.md -- has NOT been done and is owed.

Reviewed against the phase-1 boundary snapshot c68a0421, not the base commit, so phase 1's nine uncommitted files were not misattributed to this plan. Verified directly in src/shared/ics.ts that escaping happens at line-push time (104-112) and folding runs afterward (117), so folding always measures the escaped, octet-inflated value -- the one interaction neither test covers alone.

Confirmed the post-approval repair used an explicit throw-on-undefined rather than a `!` assertion or `?? ""` fallback, so an absent line still fails loudly.
